He set the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it for washing, with which Moses and Aaron and his sons washed their hands and their feet. When they went into the tent of meeting, and when they approached the altar, they washed, as the LORD commanded Moses. And he erected the court around the tabernacle and the altar, and set up the screen of the gate of the court. So Moses finished the work.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The narrator walks through the tent item by item: the frames set up, the ark placed with the testimony in it, the veil hung, the table set with bread, the lampstand lit, the incense burned, the burnt offering made, the basin filled, the court raised round it all. Seven times he stops to say as the LORD had commanded Moses. Seven acts of obedience, each closed with the same phrase, echo the sevenfold rhythm of Genesis 1, where God sees seven times that what he has made is good, and then rests.

Then So Moses finished the work, echoing Genesis 2:2, where God finished his work and rested. The book that began with slaves making bricks for a tyrant ends with a free people finishing a building for their God, in creation language.
verseByVerse.note: Israel had arrived at Sinai in the third month (19:1), so Israel spent most of a year at the mountain.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 34-38 — The Glory Fills the Tabernacle
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Verses 34-38: The glory fills the tabernacle so that Moses cannot enter, and from then on Israel moves only when the cloud moves.
verseByVerse.theology:
What the Whole Book Was Travelling Toward

God takes up residence in the middle of the camp.
verseByVerse.examples: Israel's only plan was the presence of God. A Christian's life, too, is shaped by following where he leads.

verseByVerse.quote: Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle. And Moses was not able to enter the tent of meeting because the cloud settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle. Throughout all their journeys, whenever the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the people of Israel would set out. But if the cloud was not taken up, then they did not set out till the day that it was taken up. For the cloud of the LORD was on the tabernacle by day, and fire was in it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel throughout all their journeys.
verseByVerse.commentary:
This is what the whole book has been travelling toward. Not the sea, not the mountain, not the law, but this. God said at the bush I have come down to deliver them, and at 29:46 that he brought them out that I might dwell among them, and here he arrives and takes up residence in the middle of the camp.

The first consequence: even Moses cannot go in. The man who spoke with God face to face stands outside his own tent. The glory is not tame, and the arrival of God's presence does not make God smaller.

The last three verses are the shape of every day that followed, and the book ends without arriving anywhere. Israel is not in the land but in a desert, camped round a tent, watching a cloud, and their whole itinerary is moving when it moves and staying when it stays. That is the last picture Exodus gives: a people whose only plan is the presence of God, in sight of all of them, every day.

Centuries later a man wrote of someone he had eaten and travelled with, and reached for this scene: And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we have seen his glory, glory as of the only Son from the Father (John 1:14). The verb means to pitch a tent. What filled the tabernacle so that Moses could not enter walked out of Nazareth and let people sit next to it.

And the last page of Scripture finishes the sentence. There is no temple in the city, because God himself is there (Rev. 21:22), and a loud voice says Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man. He will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God (Rev. 21:3). That is Exodus 40:34 with the tent removed, the veil gone, and nobody standing outside. The cloud in the desert was the down payment on a city where the glory needs no housing because everyone is inside it.
